headline.label: Fast memory profile
headline.plain: Your memory is running its advertised fast profile instead of the slow safe default.

headline.label: Memory speed
headline.plain: The speed stored in the BIOS profile for your memory.

headline.label: CPU tuning mode
headline.plain: The full expert menu is switched on, so every setting below is available.

headline.label: Profile saved
headline.plain: Saved on a Saturday. This file is a snapshot of the BIOS at that moment.

sections.title: Memory
sections.subtitle: How fast your memory talks to the CPU

items.name: Fast memory profile (XMP)
items.plain: One switch that loads the memory maker's tested fast settings.

items.name: Memory speed
items.plain: Bigger numbers mean the memory can hand data over faster.

items.name: Timing mode
items.plain: Linked keeps all memory sticks on the same timing rules, which is the safe choice.

items.name: Memory Try It!
items.plain: A built-in overclocking shortcut. Leaving it off means the fast profile is doing the work.

items.name: Memory extension mode
items.plain: Extra tuning for memory performance. Off is the normal, stable setting.

items.name: Retry count after a failed memory boot
items.plain: If the fast profile ever fails to start, the board tries this many times before falling back.

items.name: Fast boot
items.plain: Shortens memory training on every start. Auto lets the board decide.

sections.title: Processor
sections.subtitle: How the CPU is allowed to boost

items.name: CPU cooler profile
items.plain: Tells the board what cooling you have. It decides the power limits.

items.name: P-core ratio
items.plain: The main speed multiplier. Auto means the CPU picks its own safe boost.

items.name: E-core ratio
items.plain: The multiplier for the small efficiency cores. Auto is the normal choice.

items.name: Ratio apply mode
items.plain: All Core means every core follows the same rule.

items.name: Ring ratio
items.plain: The speed of the CPU's internal shared cache. Auto is normal.

items.name: Base clock
items.plain: The heartbeat everything else multiplies from. 100.00 is the stock value.

items.name: CPU current limit
items.plain: A safety ceiling on electrical current. Auto follows the cooler profile.

items.name: Long duration power limit
items.plain: How many watts the CPU may use for long jobs. Auto follows the cooler profile.

items.name: Short duration power limit
items.plain: How many watts the CPU may use briefly for bursty jobs.

items.name: CPU Lite Load
items.plain: How aggressively the board feeds voltage. Auto is the safe default.

sections.title: Voltages
sections.subtitle: Electrical settings that are best left alone

items.name: CPU core voltage
items.plain: Auto lets the CPU ask for exactly what it needs.

items.name: System agent voltage
items.plain: Feeds the part of the CPU that talks to memory.

items.name: CPU VDDQ voltage
items.plain: A memory-related CPU voltage.

items.name: CPU VDD2 voltage
items.plain: Another memory-related CPU voltage.

items.name: Memory voltage
items.plain: Auto follows the fast memory profile you selected.

items.name: Memory VDDQ voltage
items.plain: Memory signalling voltage.

items.name: Memory VPP voltage
items.plain: Memory activation voltage.

sections.title: Other saved details
sections.subtitle: Smaller settings stored in the same file

items.name: DMI link speed
items.plain: The link between the CPU and the chipset. Gen4 is the fastest this board supports.

items.name: Memory changed detection
items.plain: The board notices when memory has been swapped and retrains it.

items.name: Boot straight to the simple screen
items.plain: Whether the BIOS opens on its easy screen. Off means it opens in the advanced menu.
